circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, located on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, is a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke that has served as the season finale venue for Formula One since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One destinations, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track situated around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting motorsport series. This FIA Grade 1 licensed venue serves as a premier venue for international racing competition.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg, Austria, originally opened as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix continuously from 1970 through 1987. Following a renovation and shortening, the track was renamed the A1-Ring and again hosted the Austrian Grand Prix during the 1997 to 2003 period.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Situated alongside Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan's capital, the Baku City Circuit is a temporary street track spanning 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit debuted with the 2016 European Grand Prix before transitioning to host the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards under the management of the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that same year. This FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various motorsport series including GP2, drag racing, and endurance competitions, while offering multiple track configurations for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a mainstay of motorsport since hosting a Grand Prix in 1925 and competing in the inaugural Formula One season in 1950. The venue has continuously staged the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two interruptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometer temporary track that annually hosts Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport competitions including sportscar championships and North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese racing facility is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 until 2019 before resuming in 2024. In addition to hosting the main Formula One event, the circuit began featuring electric racing competitions from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near Silverstone in Northamptonshire, England, this racing venue has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with two other circuits from 1955 to 1986, the Grand Prix became permanently established here from 1987 onwards, while the track also serves as a regular stop on the MotoGP calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted Formula One's historic first Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it debuted in 1986. Originally envisioned as a street course in Budapest's central park, the venue was instead constructed as a permanent circuit outside the city, completed remarkably quickly in just eight months, faster than any other Formula One track built at that time.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located north of Milan in Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 that ranks among Europe's earliest purpose-built racing venues. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, making it one of the most enduring Formula One locations, and earned its "Temple of Speed" designation through its distinctive combination of lengthy straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka International Racing Course is a 5. 807 km motorsport facility situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, and managed by Honda Mobilityland. The venue regularly hosts both Formula One and Japanese Super Formula events, attracting a capacity crowd of 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares. The 3. 8-mile layout passes iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a unique urban racing environment in one of the world's most recognizable destinations.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304-kilometre Mexico City circuit honours two deceased racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who perished in separate racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three distinct eras, most recently becoming a regular fixture from 2015 onwards under its current branding as the Mexico City Grand Prix.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners designed specifically for Formula One racing. Since joining the calendar in 2022, the track has hosted the Miami Grand Prix with qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph, while also accommodating Formula E events on an adapted configuration beginning in 2025–26.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street layout that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, circling the harbour of the Principality of Monaco. The track is officially known as "Monte Carlo" since the majority of its course runs through that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes northwest of Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until its departure from the Formula One calendar in 2026. The venue, situated near the North Sea, had been previously known as Circuit Park Zandvoort before undergoing a rebranding in 2017.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km track featuring a 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 status.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features additional karting facilities dedicated to another celebrated Brazilian motorsport figure.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since 2021, it has been the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and it recently began hosting international electric racing competition in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated around Singapore's Marina Bay, spanning the urban districts of Downtown Core and Kallang.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km motorsport venue located near Barcelona in northeastern Spain, featuring a diverse layout combining extended straights with varied corner configurations that make it suitable for testing multiple aspects of racing performance. The facility holds an FIA Grade 1 classification and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located near Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the United States Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond F1, the track hosts multiple international racing series including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, while previously accommodating various other motorsport championships ranging from IndyCar to rally racing.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso, a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin, has secured two Formula One world titles during his 23-season career with Renault in 2005 and 2006, accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond Formula One, he has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both a Formula One world championship and a world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Italy in Formula One, driving for Mercedes since his 2025 debut. The driver has already claimed eight Grand Prix victories in his early career.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman, a British motorsport competitor, currently drives for Haas in the Formula One World Championship.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He has achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship, both during his time with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020, and has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor who currently races in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve position with Haas while pursuing his sports car racing commitments in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing. He has made limited Formula One appearances, competing across seven race weekends during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French racing driver, currently competes for Alpine in Formula One. Previously driving for AlphaTauri, he claimed victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian motorsport competitor who races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, representing France internationally.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver who races for Ferrari in Formula One, holding an unprecedented seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. The veteran competitor leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing experience from a successful career spanning multiple racing disciplines. Beyond his current series commitments, he achieved a major milestone by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently driving for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc is a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved runner-up status in the 2022 drivers' championship. Across his nine seasons, he has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who raced in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he competes in endurance racing for BMW's factory team at WRT and participates part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, where he captured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship. The driver has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories over his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver currently competing for Haas in Formula One, previously achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that has included six Grand Prix victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while competing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver currently racing for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning four seasons.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One throughout a 14-season span from 2011 until 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously driven in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, where he competes at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. After competing as a full-time Formula One driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen races for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. He has accumulated 73 race victories throughout his 12-season Formula One career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor, raced in the championship from 2022 to 2024 and currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac. He remains a pioneering figure in the sport as the only driver from his nation to have competed at the highest level of motorsport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021, Alpine has served as Renault's works team under various sponsorship arrangements. The squad, formerly known as Renault F1 Team, shifted its identity to represent the French manufacturer's Alpine sports car marque, maintaining this role until Renault's Formula One withdrawal at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has engaged in Formula One competition across multiple formats as a British manufacturer, with its present incarnation operating under AMR GP Limited as Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, participating continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. Recognizable by their iconic Prancing Horse emblem, the squad has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: The American-licensed team, founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas and debuting in 2016, competes in Formula One under the TGR Haas banner. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner, who held the position since the team's establishment until his departure in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss constructor, established in 1970, developed a successful endurance racing program before joining Formula One in 1993, where it competed as an independent team for over three decades. The organization achieved notable success in sports car racing, including victories at Le Mans and multiple world championships, before being acquired by Audi in 2024 to serve as the foundation for Audi's factory Formula One effort. The team concluded its independent operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-tenured constructors by number of races contested.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility in Surrey. The team operates as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group, which is fully owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has participated in Formula One since 1954 in various capacities as both constructor and engine supplier. The modern Mercedes-AMG Petronas team, operating from Brackley under a German licence, became a three-way partnership in January 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and team principal Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The marque's racing efforts carry the traditional "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor competing since 2024, operating as one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned squads alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with operations near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad represents the Austrian conglomerate's second Constructor entry in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two Red Bull-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operations near Milton Keynes, the team operates as a sister squad within the Red Bull motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team based in England that has operated since 2005 under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. Led by Christian Horner for two decades before Laurent Mekies took over in 2025, the team represents one of two Red Bull-owned entries in the sport. Red Bull GmbH also owns Racing Bulls, the second team under its portfolio.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial manufacturing facility in England.
